summary: Reconnect state snapback causes final sentence omission in streaming responses
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when resuming a long streaming SSE response after the mobile client is backgrounded and then restored, the last sentence of the assistant reply is sometimes missing even though server logs show the stream continued.

Observed behavior: After a reconnect and resume attempt the stream emits duplicated earlier tokens, the client deduplicator drops the overlapping suffix and the stream terminator (end marker) is not observed by the client, which results in UI showing an incomplete final sentence.

Expected behavior: Resume flow should deliver the last contiguous sequence of tokens including any closing punctuation or explicit end marker so the client receives a complete sentence and the stream terminates cleanly.

Customer impact: NimbusDocs notes frequent user-facing truncation on their mobile app during short background/foreground cycles. This affects around ~8% of streaming sessions for them according to their metrics and is blocking their launch of an in-app summarization feature.
impact: Partial outputs lead to bad UX and increased retries. Customer reports ~8% failure rate on mobile app background/resume. Dedicated customer with reserved capacity — high priority for launch timeline.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming SSE generation (chat) using redwood/gptx-3.2b on prod us-east with client_mobile SDK v1.6.2.
2) Let the assistant generate a multi-sentence paragraph (~120-200 tokens).
3) Put the mobile app into background for ~5-10s to force socket close / OS suspend.
4) Restore app to foreground and allow SDK to perform resume handshake with the server.
5) Observe client UI: sometimes final sentence(s) are missing even though server logs show tokens emitted after resume.
logs: Relevant server traces: resume request id=tr_9f2e3bd, client_resume_offset=115, server_resume_applied_offset=37, resume_state_hash mismatch logged. Worker migration events around 2026-03-10T14:03:22Z. Attached excerpts from request traces and cloudlogs query: log://prod/serving-runtime/trace/tr_9f2e3bd and dashboard link https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/resume-traces?var-trace=tr_9f2e3bd
investigation:
Initial investigation (SRE): reproduced with mobile SDK v1.6.2 on a test app. When the client resumes, it sends an offset which the resume handler accepts but an older worker instance (recently restarted / migrated) replies with a truncated prefix window due to stale KV cache. Observed behavior: the server emitted a small duplicate prefix and then emitted the remaining tokens, but the resume response did not always include the canonical stream terminator event (end-of-response marker) in the same sequence number after a duplicate overlap. Client-side deduplication removed the duplicate range and, due to an ordering edge, dropped the subsequent terminator event.

Hypothesis: race between resume accept and worker-local KV cache priming during worker migration / autoscaler scale-in leads to a transient resume-offset snapback where server reports an earlier applied offset. Client deduplicator and event coalescing presumed monotonic sequence numbers; the overlap triggers a path that discards the final end marker.

Reproduction notes: added interleaved keepalives and introduced a 200ms artificial delay on resume path; reproduces ~90% locally. Observed related metrics: increased resume_retries and resume_overlap_count in prod for NimbusDocs in the last 48h. Cross-reference channel: #support-nimbusdocs thread (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C06SUPPORT/pt2g3r8).
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Nair: Customer attached sample transcript and SDK debug logs. Provided initial triage asking for correlation ids and example timestamps.
2026-03-10 Alex Chen: Confirmed trace tr_9f2e3bd shows applied_offset less than client_resume_offset. Flagged serving-runtime resume handler and KV cache as suspects. Adding serving-runtime oncall.

2026-03-11 SRE - Maya Patel: Reproduced locally with instrumented resume path. Created minimal repro harness and validated that forcing a worker restart during resume increases likelihood. Created PR with instrumentation and locking changes (see related_github_prs).
2026-03-11 Customer (NimbusDocs): Provided prod timestamps and agrees to test a canary rollout. They are on a Dedicated contract and can accept a short maintenance window.
2026-03-12 Alex Chen: Deployed a targeted canary (serving-runtime@2026-03-12-canary-resume-fix) to 10% of NimbusDocs traffic in us-east. Monitoring initial errors and resume_overlap_count.
resolution:
Workaround: Ask customer to enable a short client-side post-resume jitter that waits for 150ms before applying deduplication window; this temporarily reduces observed omissions.

Fix rolled: Serving team implemented a guard in the resume handler to canonicalize applied_offset based on authoritative KV checkpoint and to always emit a synthetic end marker when overlap is detected. Patch deployed to canary on 2026-03-12 and promoted to full NimbusDocs pool after 2 hours of clean metrics.

Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5482. Follow-up action: add a probe test for resume ordering under worker restart and add metric resume_overlap_count alert (SLO playbook updated).
follow_up_tasks: 1) Add automated e2e test for resume ordering and worker restart to CI (assigned to eng/core).
2) Instrumentation: emit resume_state_hash and applied_offset to traces for 100% of resume attempts for 48h after rollout.
3) Update mobile SDK docs to recommend a small post-resume jitter until fix is fully rolled out to all customers.
4) Postmortem draft in Confluence and notify NimbusDocs once PM approves schedule for long-term mitigation.
